content: The provided text is a detailed description of drug interactions involving omeprazole and various other medications. 1. Patients who are treatment-experienced with atazanavir should be monitored closely when taking omeprazole, as omeprazole can interfere with hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing the levels or effects of avapritinib. Caution is advised. 2. Omeprazole increases the levels of axitinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is recommended, and caution should be exercised. 3. Omeprazole decreases the levels or effects of belumosudil by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification is advised, and the dosage of belumosudil should be increased to 200 mg orally twice daily when co-administered with proton pump inhibitors (PPIs). Close monitoring is essential. 4. Omeprazole increases the levels or effects of belzutifan by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Belzutifan is a CYP2C19 substrate, and co-administration with CYP2C19 inhibitors may heighten the risk or severity of adverse effects. Monitor for anemia and hypoxia, and adjust the belzutifan dose as clinically indicated. 5. Omeprazole enhances the gastrointestinal absorption of bismuth subsalicylate, increasing its levels. This interaction is minor and applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. 6. Blessed thistle reduces the effects of omeprazole through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This interaction is minor, theoretical, and of unknown significance. 7. Bortezomib increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 8. Bosentan decreases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 9. Omeprazole reduces the levels of bosutinib by approximately 45% due to its pH-dependent solubility. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 10. Omeprazole decreases the effects of budesonide by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. Extended-release budesonide tablets are pH-dependent, and co-administration with drugs that increase gastric pH may lead to premature dissolution, potentially altering drug release and absorption in the duodenum. 11. Butabarbital and butalbital reduce the levels or effects of omeprazole by inducing CYP2C19 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 12. Omeprazole increases the levels or effects of cannabidiol by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. Cannabidiol also increases the levels or effects of omeprazole. Dose adjustments of sensitive CYP2C19 substrates may be necessary when co-administered with cannabidiol. 13. Omeprazole decreases the effects of capecitabine through an unknown mechanism. Retrospective data suggest that elevated gastric pH caused by PPI use may impair capecitabine tablet dissolution and absorption. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 14. Carbamazepine reduces the levels or effects of omeprazole by inducing CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 metabolism. This interaction is serious, and alternative therapies should be considered. Conversely, omeprazole increases carbamazepine levels by inhibiting its metabolism. Plasma levels should be monitored when these drugs are used together. 15. Omeprazole decreases the levels or effects of carbonyl iron by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 16. Omeprazole reduces the effects of cefpodoxime and cefuroxime by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 17. Cenobamate decreases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, while increasing omeprazole levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. Dose reductions of CYP2C19 substrates may be necessary when co-administered with cenobamate. 18. Omeprazole decreases the effects of ceritinib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Alternative therapies should be considered. 19. Omeprazole increases the levels of chlordiazepoxide by inhibiting its metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 20. Omeprazole increases the levels or effects of cilostazol by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. This interaction is serious, and alternative therapies should be used. 21. Omeprazole decreases the levels or effects of ciprofloxacin through an unknown mechanism. The absorption of ciprofloxacin extended-release tablets is slightly diminished (20%) when co-administered with omeprazole. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 22. Omeprazole increases the levels or effects of citalopram by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. The maximum recommended dose of citalopram is 20 mg/day in patients taking CYP2C19 inhibitors due to the risk of QT prolongation. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 23. Omeprazole increases the levels or effects of clobazam by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Dosage adjustments may be required, as CYP2C19 inhibitors can increase exposure to N-desmethylclobazam (an active metabolite). Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 24. Omeprazole increases the levels of clomipramine and clonazepam by inhibiting their metabolism. These interactions are minor, and their clinical significance is unknown. 25. Omeprazole reduces the effects of clopidogrel by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism, which is essential for clopidogrel activation. This interaction is serious, and alternative therapies should be used. Clopidogrel efficacy may be reduced by drugs that inhibit CYP2C19. 26. Omeprazole increases the levels of clorazepate by inhibiting its metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 27. Cobicistat and conivaptan increase the levels or effects of omeprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 28. Omeprazole decreases the levels or effects of crizotinib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Drugs that elevate gastric pH may reduce crizotinib solubility and bioavailability. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 29. Omeprazole decreases the levels of cyanocobalamin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. 30. Cyclophosphamide increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 31. Long-term use of PPIs, including omeprazole, may cause hypomagnesemia, increasing the risk when co-administered with drugs that also reduce magnesium levels. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 32. Dabrafenib decreases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inducing CYP2C19 metabolism. Conversely, omeprazole reduces the levels of dabrafenib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Alternative therapies should be considered. 33. Omeprazole increases the levels or effects of dacomitinib through an unspecified mechanism. Concomitant use with PPIs decreases dacomitinib concentrations, potentially reducing its efficacy. PPIs should be avoided with dacomitinib. Alternative antacids or H2-receptor antagonists may be used, with specific timing considerations. 34. Danazol increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 35. Darifenacin decreases the levels or effects of omeprazole through an unspecified mechanism. The effectiveness of PPIs may theoretically be reduced when administered with other antisecretory agents. 36. Omeprazole decreases the levels or effects of dasatinib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Alternative therapies should be used. 37. Devil's claw reduces the effects of omeprazole through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 38. Dexamethasone decreases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 39. Omeprazole increases the levels or effects of diazepam by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Strong or moderate CYP2C19 inhibitors may decrease the rate of diazepam elimination, increasing the risk of adverse reactions. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 40. Dichlorphenamide and omeprazole both decrease serum potassium levels. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 41. Omeprazole increases the toxicity of digoxin by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Alternative therapies should be used. 42. Dronedarone and drospirenone increase the levels or effects of omeprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. These interactions are minor, and their clinical significance is unknown. 43. Efavirenz increases and decreases the levels or effects of omeprazole by affecting CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 metabolism, respectively. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 44. Elagolix increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism and decreases omeprazole levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 45. Omeprazole increases the levels of eluxadoline by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Due to incomplete information on eluxadoline metabolism, caution is advised when co-administered with strong CYP2C19 inhibitors. 46. Encorafenib both inhibits and induces CYP3A4 at clinically relevant plasma concentrations. Co-administration with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates may increase toxicity or reduce efficacy. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 47. Enzalutamide decreases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative therapies should be used. 48. Omeprazole decreases the levels of erlotinib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction is contraindicated, as drugs that alter upper gastrointestinal pH may reduce erlotinib solubility and bioavailability. 49. Omeprazole increases the levels or effects of escitalopram by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 50. Eslcarbazepine acetate increases and decreases the levels or effects of omeprazole by affecting CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 metabolism, respectively. The net effect on PPI action is unclear, and gastrointestinal symptoms should be monitored. 51. Omeprazole increases the levels of estazolam by inhibiting its metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 52. Etravirine increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Conversely, omeprazole increases etravirine levels. These interactions are minor, and their clinical significance is unknown. 53. Fedratinib increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Conversely, omeprazole increases fedratinib levels. Co-administration with dual CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 inhibitors should be avoided.
